title.narrative: UNICEF contributed to a multisectoral cholera outbreak response resulting in the end of a protracted cholera outbreak that had 34,550 cases and 719 deaths (case fatality rate of 2.1 per cent). Through procurement and prepositioning of emergency supplies, UNICEF ensured an adequate emergency supplies stocks in 100 per cent hotspot districts across the eight rural and two urban provinces affected by cholera. To reduce vaccine preventable disease outbreaks, UNICEFprovided technical and financial support resulting in effective vaccination with DTP3 containing vaccine for 94 per cent of children above the age of one. UNICEF provided technical and financial support for polio and cholera outbreaks, which also enabled persons living with disabilities access services. As a result, 4,265,483 children below 10 years (2,218,051 female and 2,047,432 male) were vaccinated. Additionally, 2,126,125 people received oral cholera vaccine (OCV) including 49.8 per cent of children under the age of 15 years
